_provenance: Issue #53 family sweep A (accessanalyzer..cloudwatch, ~120 via:none rows). Evidence for every entry: live/registry.json searched service-scoped (grep by AWS::<Service>:: prefix, cross-checked against tools/mapping-gen/namesdata-generated.json's aliases/mismatches for the TF prefix -> CFN service join), plus WebFetch of docs.aws.amazon.com CloudFormation Template Reference pages for the candidate parent's property list (folds) and raw.githubusercontent.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws provider docs for the TF resource's own description/identity (aliases and tf_only/cfn_unmodeled judgment calls). At least 15 alias/fold claims were spot-verified this way; see the sweep's PR/commit description for the list.

Folds verified against a fetched CFN property list (not guessed from the name): AWS::AccessAnalyzer::Analyzer.ArchiveRules, AWS::ApiGateway::Method.{Integration,MethodResponses}, AWS::ApiGateway::Stage.MethodSettings, AWS::ApiGateway::RestApi.Policy, AWS::ElasticLoadBalancing::LoadBalancer.AppCookieStickinessPolicy, AWS::ApplicationAutoScaling::ScalableTarget.ScheduledActions, AWS::Backup::BackupVault.{LockConfiguration,Notifications,AccessPolicy}, AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup.{LoadBalancerNames,TargetGroupARNs,NotificationConfigurations,TrafficSources,Tags}, AWS::Bedrock::Agent.{ActionGroups,AgentCollaborators,KnowledgeBases}, AWS::CloudFormation::StackSet.StackInstancesGroup, AWS::Logs::LogGroup.{DataProtectionPolicy,FieldIndexPolicies}, AWS::Logs::Destination.DestinationPolicy, AWS::Logs::DeliveryDestination.DeliveryDestinationPolicy.

aws_alb / aws_alb_target_group_attachment: legacy TF synonyms of aws_lb / aws_lb_target_group_attachment (same provider-side schema, same underlying AWS API) - same alias/fold_parent as their aws_lb_* counterparts already in overlay.json's base table; live/mapping.json already carries other same-cfn_type pairs from this exact pattern (AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::Listener, ListenerCertificate, ListenerRule, TargetGroup each already have 2 TF types mapped to them), so this is not a new pattern.

aws_cloudformation_type: left unclassified on purpose. It manages a CFN Registry type VERSION via RegisterTypeVersion/SetTypeDefaultVersion/DeregisterType, but the CFN Registry itself splits that concept across at least four types depending on the extension kind (ResourceVersion + ResourceDefaultVersion for RESOURCE types, ModuleVersion + ModuleDefaultVersion for MODULE types) - one TF resource maps to a different pair depending on user config, so no single cfn_type or fold_parent is correct without further hand splitting the TF resource's own type= argument space. A wrong single-target alias here would be exactly the false-positive risk issue #53 warns against, so this is left for a future, narrower pass rather than guessed.

aws_appstream_fleet_stack_association: AWS::AppStream::StackFleetAssociation carries a working registry entry in live/registry.json, but every handler (create/read/update/delete/list) is false - a registry-laggard type. Per taxonomy.go's own comment ('a deprecated service the registry still serves a working handler for (Pinpoint, AppStream...) is left out of this map on purpose... a TF type in that service might still get a real, working mapping'), the type-level name match is recorded here as a genuine alias; whether the pairing counts as a working mapping for the registry-laggard cohort is a downstream live/residue.go concern, not this table's.

aws_bedrockagentcore_browser: aliased to AWS::BedrockAgentCore::BrowserCustom rather than the sibling AWS::BedrockAgentCore::BrowserProfile - the TF resource's own description ('Browser provides AI agents with web browsing capabilities') matches a custom browser tool definition, not a session/profile configuration. Lower confidence than the rest of this table's aliases; flagged here for a second look if BedrockAgentCore's TF surface grows a distinct browser-profile resource later.

aws_cloudfrontkeyvaluestore_key vs aws_cloudfrontkeyvaluestore_keys_exclusive: split between cfn_unmodeled and tf_only rather than both landing in the same table, because they are different shapes of the same underlying gap - _key manages one data-plane item with its own identity (cfn_unmodeled, the aws_s3_object precedent issue #53 itself names), while _keys_exclusive is a whole-store desired-state sync construct with no identity beyond the store it targets (tf_only's association-manager kind).
